summary: Open this application's pipeline: the card held from now until the pipeline is closed - one ticket's rental with a coordinator, the machine's lock without one - so that no model switch and no pause between two requests lets another application in. `models` are loaded as soon as the card is had, one at a time, side by side, and kept (pinned): the idle sweep never takes them off, and no other model's load takes them off to make room. Each is named once, and a pipeline keeps at most as many models as the runner keeps on the card at once (`max_loads`, 8 - a rental names at most 8 processes; one, when its settings name one port for every model). `class` is the ticket's: `responsive`, the default, or `scheduled`. `label` is a word for the operator. `keep_s`: a pipeline not renewed (`/api/pipeline/renew`) for that many seconds lapses, which closes it as a close would; 0 holds it until it is closed or the server stops; not named, the runner's settings say (`pipeline_keep_s`, 120). The answer comes at once, the pipeline `waiting` until it holds the card - and health carries its state from then on - unless it is asked to wait: `?wait_s=N`, a plain number of seconds from 0 to 60, holds the answer until every model it names answers its health check (`up`) or its load failed (`why` says which), until it holds the card when it names none, or until N seconds have passed, whichever comes first; an application knows the moment its models are ready without asking again and again. A wait on a server that stops is answered at once. Without an open pipeline the queue opens one of its own for its work, and closes it once the work is done; an open that finds it takes it over, card and all, and answers `holding`. One pipeline at a time: another open is refused while one is open. Any other `wait_s` is refused `bad_wait`. A `scheduled` pipeline whose first model does not fit when it takes the card either waits for room - not holding the card meanwhile: a coordinator passes its ticket over, and a server run on its own lets the machine's lock go and reads the card again until it fits - within the server's patience, the pipeline `waiting` and its `why` saying the numbers it waits on, or fails at once, `no_room`, in the loud words a responsive one does: `if_no_room`, `wait` or `fail`, says which for this pipeline; without it, the server's own (`scheduled_if_no_room` in its runner settings, `wait` unless set there). Responsive work is now: a responsive pipeline that names `if_no_room: wait` is refused `live_is_now` (S18). A pipeline names no time to start at: it is the card held now - work planned for later is a batch job with a `not_before`.
